highlights.title: Revisiting the Neutrino Emission and Physical Parameter Constraints from Time-Resolved Spectra of Gamma-Ray Bursts
highlights.reason: The paper quantitatively revises IceCube neutrino yields and jet-parameter bounds for bright GRBs by replacing duration-averaged spectra with time-resolved spectra, directly relevant to relativistic jets and high-energy neutrinos.

highlights.title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
highlights.reason: Paper directly constrains FRB source population via CHIME Catalog 2 source-count growth (linear β_s, β_r) and repeat clustering, yielding rate index α ≃ 2 and requiring long-term on/off activity rather than stationary clustering.

highlights.title: Detection of 2 MeV spectral bump and ~40 MeV emission line from GRB 221009A
highlights.reason: Unsaturated 2–255 MeV spectroscopy of GRB 221009A directly constrains prompt jet composition, separating a sub-dominant photosphere from magnetically powered emission and an evolving MeV annihilation line.

highlights.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
highlights.reason: The work targets the pre-plateau luminosity peak of SNe IIP, contrasting shock propagation in a steep hydrogen-envelope density gradient with a massive CSM shell, which is directly useful for shock-breakout, plateau, and progenitor-structure studies.

highlights.title: What the X-ray Emission from Young Supernovae Can Tell Us About Their Progenitors
highlights.reason: This review directly links young-supernova X-rays to progenitor winds, shock–CSM interaction, and pre-explosion mass-loss history, and it provides scaling relations that can test those hypotheses.

highlights.title: Jet energetics and remnant magnetism in short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron-star mergers: A statistical study via broadband afterglow modeling
highlights.reason: This statistical afterglow study directly constrains sGRB jet energy and the horizon magnetic field of BNS-merger black holes, which is central to relativistic-jet and compact-remnant engine physics. The reported $E_{\rm k}$, $\eta_\gamma$ and $B_{\rm BH}$ distributions can test whether a Blandford–Znajek engine is viable.

highlights.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
highlights.reason: Paper directly simulates simultaneous BZ jet and BP wind launching from thin accretion disks using resistive GRMHD, yielding quantitative power ratios, geometries and efficiencies relevant to relativistic outflows around compact objects.

highlights.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
highlights.reason: This is the largest uniform optical sample of thermonuclear SNe Ia-CSM and directly constrains CSM-interaction timescales, radiated energy, and the underlying Ia engine. It is relevant to SN–CSM interaction studies but is not a high-energy, jet, neutrino, or shock-breakout result.

highlights.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
highlights.reason: The paper forecasts how ultra-high-energy neutrino flavor ratios constrain isotropic Lorentz-invariance violation, which is relevant to high-energy neutrino observations, but it does not treat compact-object engines, jets, FRBs, or supernova source physics.

highlights.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
highlights.reason: This stellar-mass black-hole X-ray-binary study is adjacent to compact-object high-energy spectroscopy and photoionization, but it does not address FRBs, supernova engines, relativistic jets, or neutrinos. It is still useful for the sub-Eddington self-shadowing claim, the reflection fraction, and the $H/R$ scale.

highlights.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
highlights.reason: A geometric dust-scattering distance to the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 rescales its luminosity, Eddington ratio, mass and relativistic-jet Lorentz factor, which is useful for compact-object high-energy work but peripheral to FRB/supernova-engine studies.

highlights.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
highlights.reason: The paper quantitatively tests whether supernova fallback, neutrino emission, and explosion asymmetry give neutron stars and black holes different natal kicks, which is relevant to compact-object formation engines, but it does not directly address FRBs, shock breakout, circumstellar interaction, or jets.

highlights.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
highlights.reason: The paper gives a gauge-invariant leading-order correction to magnetic reconnection in zero-angular-momentum accretion plasma around a spherical compact object, relevant to dissipation near compact objects, but it does not treat FRBs, jet radiation, supernovae, or neutrinos.

highlights.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
highlights.reason: Reports NICER observations of a faint thermonuclear burst from the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4–3658 showing burst-driven changes to inner-disk geometry and visible neutron-star area, relevant to compact-object high-energy observations.

highlights.title: Energetic Particle Confinement In Black Hole Accretion Disks
highlights.reason: The paper is relevant to relativistic jet sheaths and compact-object neutrino emission, especially the NGC 1068 corona, but it is an incremental GRMHD tracer study of steady SMBH ADAFs rather than a direct FRB, supernova-engine, or CSM-shock result.

highlights.title: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
highlights.reason: This is a null but quantitative electron-neutrino coincidence search for LVK compact-object mergers, directly relevant to neutrinos from compact remnants, though it does not address FRB, supernova-engine, shock, or jet physics.

highlights.title: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
highlights.reason: This VLA study quantifies a recurring frequency-dependent radio lag in Sgr A* and links it to a mildly relativistic outflow, which is relevant to compact-object jet timing but is outside the group's core FRB, supernova-engine, and dispersion-measure problems.

highlights.title: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
highlights.reason: The two late TDE radio rebrightenings give quantitative outflow, jet, and circumstellar-density constraints relevant to relativistic outflows and CSM interaction, but they are incremental relative to the group's core FRB, supernova-engine, and neutrino focus.

highlights.title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
highlights.reason: This MHD-PIC study of self-regulated cosmic-ray electron DSA at a high-Mach quasi-parallel shock is useful for SNR shock spectra and magnetic amplification, but it is not directly about FRBs, central engines, shock breakout, jets, or neutrinos.

highlights.title: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
highlights.reason: This is a quantitative hard-state neutron-star X-ray study linking a 30 keV Suzaku feature in Aql X-1 to rp-process ashes, so it is relevant to compact-object high-energy observations, but it does not address FRBs, supernova engines, jets, neutrinos, shocks, or dispersion measure.

highlights.title: 3D radiative transfer of K-series lines of He-like ions with SKIRT
highlights.reason: This is a 3D Monte Carlo radiative-transfer method for He-like K-series lines in photoionized gas around compact objects, including P Cygni profiles seen by XRISM, so it is useful for photoionization and compact-object high-energy spectroscopy but is not a direct FRB, supernova-engine, jet, or neutrino result.

highlights.title: EP250226a: A fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A and its multiwavelength afterglow properties
highlights.reason: This is a high-redshift Einstein Probe fast X-ray transient coincident with a classical long GRB, with quantitative afterglow constraints on jet energy, radiative efficiency, and ISM versus wind circumburst medium.

highlights.title: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
highlights.reason: The paper develops a rigorous scattering-order Stokes recursion and asymptotic eigenmode formalism for polarized transport in Thomson slabs, providing essential theoretical tools to model polarized Comptonization in compact object accretion coronae such as the neutron star X-ray binary 4U 1624–49 observed by IXPE.

highlights.title: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
highlights.reason: This work establishes a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) pipeline to classify and inspect emission mechanisms across $36{,}904$ Chandra ACIS X-ray detections, providing useful methodology for compact object high-energy source classification and jet knot diagnostics.

highlights.title: The $w$-mode instability of strangeon ergostars and its impact on energy extraction
highlights.reason: Investigates whether non-axisymmetric $w$-mode instabilities deplete the rotational energy reservoir of strangeon ergostars as alternative sGRB central engines, finding them dynamically stable along maximum-energy-extraction paths.

highlights.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
highlights.reason: The paper targets the ANITA-IV upward air-shower versus IceCube null ultra-high-energy neutrino tension, so it is relevant to high-energy neutrino observations, but its dark-sector mass flip-flop is peripheral to FRB, supernova-engine, and jet studies.

entries.title: Spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries
entries.abstract: It is well-known that in the merger of a black-hole binary with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, the spin of the final black hole always increases with the spin of the components. We show that this very intuitive behavior is violated in black hole--neutron star binaries, where the spin of the final black hole actually decreases as the spin of the neutron star increases. Using a large set of binaries with different spins and mass ratios, we identify the mechanism behind this surprising result in the nonlinear dynamics of the tidal disruption, which drives a substantial loss of angular momentum via dynamical ejecta, in some cases comparable to that radiated via gravitational waves. Our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

entries.title: galpy with differentiable, accelerated backends: galactic dynamics in jax and PyTorch
entries.abstract: We describe an extension of galpy, the Python library for galactic dynamics, that adds jax and PyTorch as computational backends alongside its existing numpy and C implementation. With it, galpy's gravitational potentials, orbit integration, action-angle transformations and their inverses, and distribution functions, including those for tidal streams, run on GPUs, can be compiled as part of a user's program, and can be differentiated with respect to their inputs and parameters, from the force at a point to the samples drawn from a distribution function. The user-facing design is kept simple: the active backend follows from the type of the arrays that are passed in, the galpy interface is unchanged, and the numpy path gives the same results as before. We describe the design of the backend framework and its implementation in each of galpy's modules, with examples of use, and we discuss its limitations. On a GPU, batches of orbits, samples from distribution functions, and stream models run one to five orders of magnitude faster than on a single CPU core. To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural network trained through galpy. An AI coding agent wrote essentially all of the code under the detailed direction and review of the human author, and we describe how we organized this work and how we established the correctness of the result. This work is the start of galpy's version 2, which is available at https://github.com/jobovy/galpy and documented at https://docs.galpy.org/en/v2/ .

entries.title: Early-Excess SNe Ia Show Strong C II Absorption
entries.abstract: Some type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit an early excess in their rising light curves, but the physical origin of this behavior remains uncertain. The processes driving these excesses affect the ejecta at early times and may also imprint on the outermost layers. We investigate whether early excesses are associated with differences in unburned material by measuring pre-maximum carbon absorption. Using multi-component Gaussian fits to the blended Si II $\lambda6355$ and C II $\lambda6580$ region, we measure pseudo-equivalent widths and velocities for a sample of 35 nonpeculiar SNe Ia with rising light curve categorizations. We find that early-excess objects ($n=13$) tend to exhibit stronger C II absorption than non-excesses ($n=22$) at phases earlier than approximately $-13$ d, with a two-sample K-S test of the earliest measurements yielding $p=0.025$. In contrast, the HV Si II components do not clearly separate the two groups. Early-excess SNe Ia tend to be more luminous and decline more slowly, but objects with similar maximum-light properties span a range of C II pseudo-equivalent widths, suggesting that this effect is distinct from the known luminosity-width relation. We show that, at least in some cases, when objects have similar light-curve shape and photospheric temperature, the effect we see is not driven by ionization but by distinct differences in the explosion, such as carbon abundance and density and the efficiency of burning in the WD. Our results provide a new constraint on SN Ia explosion models for early excesses, as they must produce a tendency for stronger early C II absorption.

entries.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
entries.abstract: We present the largest uniform study to date of 50 thermonuclear Type Ia supernovae interacting with circumstellar medium (SNe Ia-CSM). As the first paper in a series delineating the population properties of this class, this work focuses specifically on a uniform analysis of their light curves. Our results show that SNe Ia-CSM display a significantly more uniform light-curve morphology than interacting core-collapse SNe IIn, closely resembling the luminous-slow subgroup. The Ia-CSM sample spans approximately an order of magnitude in peak luminosity, total timescale, and radiated energy, with a median optical peak luminosity of $\approx2\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ ($\approx-20$ mag). We find a distinct bimodality in the radiated energy distribution: a predominant population of energetic events with $\approx 2\times10^{50}$ erg and characteristic timescales of $\approx100$ days, and a secondary population that is roughly an order of magnitude less energetic with shorter timescales of $\approx50$ days. Decomposition of the luminosity contributions from underlying SN Ia and CSM interaction by the Ia-CSM spectral classification reveals a diverse range of underlying SN Ia subtypes spanning from luminous 1991T-like to faint 1991bg-like. Both SN Ia and CSM properties are broadly consistent with the core-degenerate channel resulting from common-envelope evolution followed by core merger, where the presence of dense CSM is dictated by the delay time between the common-envelope phase and the thermonuclear explosion. Subsequent papers in this series will utilize numerical simulations, semi-analytical modeling, spectroscopy, and host-galaxy environments to further constrain the progenitor and explosion pathways to SNe Ia-CSM.

entries.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
entries.abstract: Neutrino flavor measurements test physics beyond the Standard Model that modifies neutrino production, propagation, or detection. IceCube has measured the flavor composition of the astrophysical neutrino flux up to PeV energies. Next-generation experiments will extend flavor measurements to the ultra-high-energy (UHE) regime, $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$-$10\,\mathrm{EeV}$, by combining in-ice radio detection with Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. We present the first study of the new-physics reach of these projected UHE flavor measurements. We take Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) as a benchmark, since its effects grow as a power of the neutrino energy. We find that UHE flavor ratios will be the most sensitive probe of LIV for operators of dimension four and higher, improving on current bounds from all sectors by up to twenty orders of magnitude. Three-flavor observables improve this sensitivity by up to an order of magnitude over Earth-skimming tau neutrinos alone.

entries.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
entries.abstract: Accretion onto black holes powers some of the most energetic sources in the Universe, yet its behaviour across the luminosity range remains poorly understood. Specifically, as the luminosity approaches the Eddington limit ($L_{\rm Edd}$), the inner accretion disk is expected to depart from the standard thin-disk solution, becoming vertically extended. The luminosity threshold and observational signatures of this transition remain, however, uncertain. We present multiwavelength spectroscopy obtained during the decay of a black hole X-ray binary outburst. At the peak ($\sim 0.2\,L_{\rm Edd}$), a cool optical and near-infrared spectrum dominated by strong recombination lines of hydrogen and He I is observed. However, as the luminosity decreases, it switches to a hot, highly irradiated, nearly featureless spectrum. This puzzling behavior reveals the emergence of a vertically extended inner disk at the outburst peak, shielding the outer regions from high-energy radiation produced near the black hole; a scenario supported by contemporaneous X-ray spectra. Observations of similar systems suggest that this phenomenon may be common among black hole accretion disks. Self-shadowing structures at luminosities well below $L_{\rm Edd}$ have major implications for black hole accretion flows and their observational properties, affecting inferred black hole spins, X-ray polarization measurements, and the physical conditions of the outer disk and its associated outflows.

entries.title: Post-adiabatic effects sourced by radiation reaction for inspiraling, eccentric binaries in post-Newtonian theory
entries.abstract: The adiabatic approximation, in which eccentric binaries evolve under orbit-averaged fluxes, is widely used in gravitational-wave and astrophysical modeling. We use resummed multiple-scale analysis, which is closely related to near-identity averaging transformations, to derive post-adiabatic corrections from leading-order radiation reaction and explain how the accuracy of the adiabatic approximation depends on the initial orbital phase. While the secular evolution equations for the eccentricity and semi-major axis receive no explicit first post-adiabatic corrections, their solutions acquire such corrections through the initial conditions. We also derive the change in the functional form of the gravitational-wave polarizations that cancels the gauge dependence of the orbital elements at first post-adiabatic order, ensuring agreement between waveforms evaluated at the same physical event in different coordinates. At a radial turning point, the first post-adiabatic oscillations of the semi-major axis and eccentricity vanish, so the initial osculating energy and angular momentum agree with their orbit-averaged values up to second post-adiabatic corrections. When initialized elsewhere along the orbit, the adiabatic approximation can accumulate significant dephasing, which the first post-adiabatic approximation can substantially reduce. Both dephasings can change sign across parameter space, consistent with competing contributions from successive orders. Accounting for initialization is therefore essential for assessing the accuracy of these approximations, particularly for long-lived, highly eccentric binaries.

entries.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
entries.abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

entries.title: Beyond classification: regressing physical merger properties using solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum
entries.abstract: Galaxy mergers play an important role in galaxy evolution; they enhance star formation, transform morphologies, and may drive accretion onto black holes. Due to their complex morphological features, identification of mergers poses a significant challenge. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successful at identifying mergers with good accuracy. However, similar to other deep learning techniques such as Vision Transformers, they require large training samples. Current methods are also limited to classification, rather than regression. Here, we apply the solid harmonic wavelet scattering bispectrum, a method that encodes invariances and symmetries in the data which need to be learned by CNNs, as an alternative to CNNs. We apply our methodology to a simulated dataset of galaxies with a wide range of merger properties. We show that this method outperforms standard methodologies, while requiring fewer training samples and being robust to noise. Most importantly, we show that for the first time this method is able to regress on both merger mass ratio and time since merger simultaneously, with uncertainties ~ 0.33 dex uncertainty in merger mass ratio and ~ 0.66 Gyr uncertainty in time since merger. We have therefore shown that solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum presents an alternative to currently used machine learning techniques.

entries.title: Observational constraints on CO sequestration and disk mass in the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk
entries.abstract: Exoplanets accrete gas, dust, and ice from their natal environment, setting the chemical composition of their atmospheres and interiors. The abundance of the major volatiles in disks can be used to possibly link exoplanet atmospheres to their formation location in the disk. In this work, we aim to quantify the peak CO abundance and disk mass of the PDS 70 disk, the first disk with a direct confirmation of two accreting planets in its dust cavity. We present the first detection of N$_2$H$^+$ and C$^{17}$O in this disk. The C$^{17}$O emission shows marginal statistical evidence for an azimuthal asymmetry trailing that previously seen in the continuum emission. We then compare the disk integrated fluxes of N$_2$H$^+$, CO isotopologues, and the continuum to an existing grid of thermochemical models. We find that the derived disk mass drops by a factor of $\sim 3.4$ from $0.039^{+0.067}_{-0.018}$ M$_{\odot}$ to $0.011^{+0.011}_{-0.006}$ M$_{\odot}$ if the C$^{17}$O line flux is included in the fitting procedure; the quoted intervals do not include systematic uncertainties. CO on the other hand is sequestered with an effective abundance of $(4.8^{+4.3}_{-2.7} - 17^{+8}_{-8}) \times 10^{-6}$ relative to H$_2$ in the probed disk layers after accounting for CO freeze-out and isotope selective CO photodissociation for the adopted chemical network and ionization prescription. The range in peak CO abundances reflects the uncertainty in the N$_2$H$^+$ emission, assuming either optically thin emission at 21 K or optically thick emission. Therefore, the PDS 70 planets are possibly accreting the final portion of their atmospheres from the outer disk molecular layer where CO is sequestered. Thus, CO sequestering may need to be considered when interpreting the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres.

entries.title: FRIDA: Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies. I. Programme overview, resolved gas density profiles, and HI mass-size relation
entries.abstract: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) provide powerful tests of galaxy formation models at low surface densities. However, the structure of their neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) remains poorly constrained, hampering our understanding of this population. We present FRIDA (Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies), a MeerKAT and VLA programme providing high-resolution HI data of 12 gas-rich UDGs. In this paper, we introduce our sample and delve into the associated observations and data reduction. We derive HI fluxes, masses ($M_{\rm HI}$), and resolved surface density profiles ($Σ_{\rm HI}(R)$). We find extended ($\sim 7-30\ \rm{kpc}$ in radius) and regular HI emission in our UDGs, and we report the discovery of a satellite around one of them. Most UDGs in FRIDA have $Σ_{\rm HI}(R)$ profiles with flat inner parts reaching $Σ_{\rm HI}(R)\approx 4\ M_\odot\ \rm{pc^{-2}}$ near their centres, which then decline exponentially in their outer parts. By modelling the HI morphology of the UDGs, we find a median inclination of $43^\circ$, in agreement with theoretical expectations for disc galaxies under UDG selection effects. Moreover, we place our UDGs in the $M_{\rm HI}-R_{\rm HI}$ and $M_{\rm HI}-R_{\rm 50,HI}$ mass-size relations, where $R_{\rm HI}$ is radius at which $Σ_{\rm HI}(R)=1\ M_\odot \rm{pc^{-2}}$, and $R_{\rm 50,HI}$ is the radius enclosing $50\%$ of $M_{\rm HI}$. While our UDGs lie within the scatter of the relations, they systematically fall on their upper side, being slightly (by $\sim 15-25\%$) more extended and of lower mean $Σ_{\rm HI}$ (by $\sim 25-35\%$) than average galaxies at similar $M_{\rm HI}$. Moreover, we find that $Σ_{\rm HI}(R/R_{\rm HI})$ and $M_{\rm HI}(<R)/M_{\rm HI}$ for UDGs follow an intermediate trend between late-type discs and early-type galaxies, with a large overlap with Sa galaxies.

entries.title: Dark matter alters dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies
entries.abstract: Dwarf galaxies are the most dark-matter-dominated systems in the Universe, serving as unique laboratories for exploring the fundamental nature of the dark sector. Although the observed diversity in dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies suggests an interplay between dark matter and baryonic physics, this relationship has remained largely unquantified in existing models. Here, we utilize a set of novel cosmological simulations with baryons to demonstrate how dark matter physics directly drives the structural evolution of these galaxies. By comparing the same systems across cold dark matter and varied self-interacting dark matter models, we find that the evolution of the central density of dark matter significantly impacts a galaxy's half-light radius, but the signal is dependent on morphology. This causal link establishes galaxy size as a direct signature of the underlying dark matter microphysics. Our findings provide a predictive framework for decoding dark matter particle properties from galactic shapes, offering a roadmap for upcoming wide-field surveys, such as the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, to probe the dark sector through the statistical analysis of galaxy populations.

entries.title: Variations in the Extinction Curve at High Galactic Latitudes as seen by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument
entries.abstract: The dust extinction curve, characterized by the total-to-selective extinction ratio, $R(V)$, varies with grain size and composition. Accurate $R(V)$ values are crucial for dereddening astronomical colors and understanding the interstellar medium. We measure extinction toward stars with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy using a machine-learning-based relative of the "pair method," matching reddened and unreddened stars. We use XGBoost to predict stars' intrinsic colors from their spectroscopic parameters ($T_\mathrm{eff}$, $\log g$, $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$) and subtract them from observed colors to measure reddening in combinations of the $g$, $r$, $z$, $W1$, and $W2$ bands. This approach directly measures reddening, unlike the common thermal-emission-based method of Schlegel et al. (1998; SFD). The reddening is accurate to roughly 0.02 mag in $g-r$ and $r-z$. We develop a forward model to map $g-r$ and $g-W1$ reddenings to $R(V)$ and find significant variation in $R(V)$, with $σ_\mathrm{NMAD}(R(V)) = 0.23$, in dusty regions ($E(g-r) > 0.1$) at high Galactic latitudes observed by DESI. In this footprint, $R(V)$ is bimodal, with modes at 2.9 and 3.4, likely due to large-spatial-scale correlations in the shape of the extinction curve combined with the relatively small number of distinct sightlines with substantial reddening. We find no strong relationship between $R(V)$ and other tracers of the interstellar medium, such as thermal emission, dust temperature, spectral emissivity index $β$, and $Hα$. However, the error in the SFD-predicted extinction correlates well with $R(V)$, implying that a single optical reddening combined with the far-infrared dust brightness can predict variations in the extinction curve.

entries.title: Tracing Galactic Dust Reddening with Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission: SPHEREx Observations of the North Ecliptic Pole
entries.abstract: We investigate the ability of SPHEREx observations of the $3.3$ $μ$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission feature to trace Galactic dust reddening. Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the $3.3$ $μ$m PAH feature in each $6''.2$ pixel of a $22^{\circ}$ by $22^{\circ}$ region centered on the north ecliptic pole (NEP). We convert the PAH feature strength to reddening by applying a radiation field correction and a linear scale factor. The resulting $E(B-V)$ map is consistent with far-infrared, stellar, and HI-based reddening maps at arcminute scales, exhibiting a typical $E(B-V)$ difference of $\lesssim 7$ mmag. A galaxy count test finds that all reddening maps have a dispersion of $\approx11$ mmag in $E(B-V)$ relative to what would be needed to produce spatially uniform galaxy counts. While there is some evidence that reddening is overestimated by our map at high PAH abundances, this effect is smaller than the uncertainties on the applied radiation field corrections and limited to $\sim$10 mmag in the most extreme regions of the NEP. For a diffuse, high Galactic latitude region like the NEP and at the sensitivities of our validation metrics, the SPHEREx PAH-emission based reddening map matches the accuracy of existing reddening maps while being capable of accessing a higher angular resolution of $\sim6''$.

entries.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
entries.abstract: We derived a geometrical distance of the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 based on X-ray dust-scattering rings associated with its 1992 and 2002 outbursts. We analyzed archival ROSAT and XMM-Newton observations and identified an X-ray dust-scattering ring in each observation, produced by two different dust layers along the line of sight. By combining the angular radii of the rings with the independently determined distances of the scattering dust layers and the epochs of the corresponding outbursts, we derive a best-constrained distance to 4U 1543-475 of 4.6 $\pm$ 0.2 kpc. This value is substantially smaller than the distance of 7.5 kpc commonly adopted in the literature and has important implications for the inferred physical properties of the system. In particular, the revised distance favors the presence of a low-mass extended-horizontal-branch donor star over a main-sequence star, calling for a reassessment of the dynamical parameters of the binary and, consequently, of the black-hole mass. The smaller distance also affects the inferred properties of the relativistic jet and the estimate of black-hole spin derived from the spectral continuum-fitting.

entries.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: I. Population Synthesis Framework and Illustrative Examples
entries.abstract: The natal kicks imparted to neutron stars and black holes at birth are critical for understanding massive-star evolution, compact-object formation, and compact binary merger rates. However, constraining these kicks is challenging, since they cannot be directly observed. Here, we outline a framework for inferring natal kick probability distributions for compact binaries. Our method embeds the rapid binary-population code COSMIC in a Monte-Carlo workflow that evolves ensembles of simulated binaries. From those which host compact objects, we can select subsets that match the observational characteristics of any given system (e.g. component masses, orbital period, mass-transfer status, systemic velocity). As a proof-of-concept, we apply this framework to six compact binaries spanning a wide range of companion masses and compact-object types. For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space. We reconfirm that at least one black hole system, XTE J1118+480, must have received a natal kick $v_{\rm NK} > 100$ km s$^{-1}$. The neutron-star system, GX 301-2, is also inferred to have received an impulsive kick exceeding 280 km s$^{-1}$. We discuss the strengths and limitations associated with population-synthesis-based inference methods and explore the effects of adopting different prescriptions for critical binary evolution phases. We provide a detailed demonstration of the non-linear relationship between $v_{\rm NK}$ and $v_{\rm sys}$, highlighting the shortcomings of relying on observations alone to measure natal kicks. The inferred kick velocity distributions across our benchmark sample are generally consistent with previous constraints.

entries.title: On the Excitation of Sloshing Oscillations in Hot Coronal Loops
entries.abstract: Observations of hot coronal loops have often shown the presence of compressive plasma oscillations. These oscillations are usually preceded by a flare-associated localised brightening in the vicinity of one of the footpoints of the coronal loop. The flare heating produces an impulsive injection of plasma into the coronal loop, along with a plasma perturbation that bounces back and forth between the two footpoints, termed as sloshing oscillations. While the association of these oscillations with flares is apparent, the pertinent connection between their excitation and the flare characteristics remains poorly understood. In this study, using data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present a unique set of observations, where the response of a single coronal loop due to repeated flares in the same active region is evident. Our analysis reveals that in three out of five flare events, sloshing oscillations are triggered, while in the other two events, only plasma flows are observed. By examining the duration of plasma injection associated with each flare, we find that sloshing oscillations occur when the injection duration is shorter than the travel time of the plasma perturbation across the loop. In contrast, no oscillations are observed when the injection duration is comparable to the travel time. These results reveal the dependence of sloshing oscillation excitation on the temporal characteristics of flares.

entries.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
entries.abstract: Natal kicks - kinematic impulses to neutron stars and black holes at birth - play a decisive role in the end-stage evolution of binaries hosting massive stars, in determining the global phase-space properties of compact objects, and in setting expected merger-rates detectable through gravitational-wave observations. Inferring the kick ($v_{\rm NK}$) for individual systems requires well constrained binary system properties and centre-of-mass kinematics, which must then be modelled to constrain likely system characteristics at supernova. As a result, population-wide studies of kicks remain few and far between. Here, we model plausible evolutionary histories for 68 accreting binaries, encompassing almost all black-hole and neutron-star X-ray binaries with 3D kinematics measurements, constraining allowed $v_{\rm NK}$ distributions for each source using a simulation framework presented in our previous paper. The resultant $v_{\rm NK}$ distribution for the sample can be simply represented by a broad Gamma distribution with mean $v_{\rm NK}$ = $128^{+17}_{-15}$ km s$^{-1}$ and scatter $σ$ = 117 km s$^{-1}$. Intriguingly, the distributions for black-hole vs. neutron-star systems are found to be formally indistinguishable. Despite still being limited by small-number statistics, we find that black holes can receive large natal kicks, and that kicks for all remnant types span similar ranges (0-700 km s$^{-1}$). There is a hint, but no statistically significant evidence at present, for $v_{\rm NK}$ scaling inversely with black-hole mass. Our work suggests either that similar physics drives kicks and shows evidence for effects beyond simplistic fallback-moderated scaling for black holes, or that selection effects conspire to erase differences between remnant types in current accreting-binary samples. Larger samples are needed to provide robust discriminatory tests between these possibilities.

entries.title: Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems
entries.abstract: Gaia DR4 will, for the first time, provide epoch astrometry. When analysing these data, binary sources must be treated carefully, as modelling their astrometry as single stars can bias parallax and proper motion estimates. We developed the vimbinary tool, a framework to simulate and interpret epoch astrometry of unresolved binary systems and to evaluate the impact of model assumptions on the resulting astrometric parameters. We simulated Gaia DR4-like epoch astrometry for a sample of 17 well-characterised unresolved binary systems, including both non-pulsating binaries and systems containing one photometric variable component - variability-induced movers (VIMs). We show that both binary motion and the VIM effect can significantly impact parallax and proper motion measurements, with the magnitude of the effect strongly dependent on the orbital period, photocentric amplitude, and flux ratio of the specific system. We also show that larger time coverage does not necessarily improve parallax precision, in contrast to proper motion, for which precision generally improves with longer baselines. Instead, parallaxes retrieved with binary-system fitting are more accurate than those obtained within the single-star framework.

entries.title: DIISC-VIII: Chemical Signatures of Gas Accretion in Star-Forming Galaxies
entries.abstract: We investigate anomalously low-metallicity (ALM) star-forming regions in 11 galaxies from the Deciphering the Interplay between the Interstellar Medium, Stars, and the Circumgalactic Medium (DIISC) survey. We combine optical spectroscopy of 542 H$α$-bright regions from MMT/Binospec with imaging from the Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope and H I 21 cm imaging from the Very Large Array. We find 75 ALM regions: 19 identified using deviations from each galaxy's radial metallicity gradient, 27 using the resolved mass--metallicity relation (rMZR), and 29 via both methods. Regions identified by both methods are metal-poor relative to their galactocentric positions and local stellar mass surface densities by $>$ 0.1 dex, making them the strongest candidates for localized metallicity dilution. We estimate accreted masses of $5.6<\log(M_{\rm acc}/{\rm M_\odot})<7.5$ for the 48 radial-gradient-selected regions, comparable to observed and simulated high-velocity cloud masses. We calculate a mean hydrogen accretion rate of $1.02\ {\rm M_\odot yr^{-1}}$ per galaxy, which is comparable to the mean star formation rate of the sample. The strongest ALM candidates lie within or near $R_{25}$, while rMZR-only regions dominate the outer population. We find no evidence that circumgalactic Ly$α$ absorption along a single sightline traces disk chemical structure, as quantified by either the radial metallicity gradient or the fraction of radial-gradient-selected ALM regions. These results suggest that localized accretion of low-metallicity gas can sustain star formation in galaxies and demonstrate that ALM regions provide a spatially resolved indirect view of ongoing gas cycling.

entries.title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
entries.abstract: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

entries.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
entries.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

entries.title: The Gaia-alerted 2024--2025 brightening of V346 Nor
entries.abstract: Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass--accretion rate product $M_{\star}\dot{M}$ and the line-of-sight extinction $A_V$ are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher ($M_{\star}\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}^2\,$yr$^{-1}$) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from $A_V \approx 20$\,mag to $10$\,mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2\% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in H$α$ indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

entries.title: La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity
entries.abstract: Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of $\sim 85$ kpc, has a long dimension of $\sim 57^\circ$ ($\sim 85$ kpc), and a width that varies from $\sim 10^\circ $ ($\sim 15$ kpc) to $\sim 35^\circ $ ($\sim 50$ kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by $\sim 35^\circ$ from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of $0.59$ days, and only $19\pm 3 \%$ lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and $1 σ$ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger \citep{chandra2023} is supported by the $\sim 70^\circ$ angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

entries.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
entries.abstract: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near )a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter $\barκ \equiv r_sΔy^2/r^3$, where $r$ is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, $r_s$ is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and $Δy$ is the mesoscale length.

entries.title: Turbulence Properties of Corotating Interaction Regions at 1 AU: a Comprehensive Superposed Epoch Analysis
entries.abstract: We perform a comprehensive superposed epoch analysis (SEA) of more than 200 corotating interaction regions (CIRs) using WIND spacecraft observations at 1 AU. The stream interfaces are identified by Minimum Variance Analysis (MVA), and turbulence properties are evaluated using wavelet transforms over a wide range of temporal scales. The analysis of normalized cross helicity ($σ_c$) and normalized residual energy ($σ_r$) reveals distinct turbulence behaviors across frequencies. The spectral indices of both magnetic and velocity fluctuations smoothly transition from steeper in the slow wind to shallower in the fast wind, while a localized steepening of the velocity spectra near the interface indicates enhanced dissipation due to compression. Across broad frequency bands, $σ_c$ shows a clear dip at the stream interface, signifying increased inward Alfvén wave energy, whereas $σ_r$ displays a peak-valley-peak structure mainly driven by large-scale velocity shear. In lower-frequency ranges, velocity shear artificially enhances velocity fluctuation energy, producing strong peaks in $σ_r$, while higher-frequency ranges show a smooth increase of $σ_r$ from slow wind to fast wind. Nearly half of the analyzed CIRs are accompanied by a heliospheric current sheet (HCS), with many HCSs closely aligned with the stream interface, suggesting an intrinsic link between the two structures. Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.

entries.title: How Intensity Threshold Shapes the Velocity Dispersion-Size Relation in Molecular Clouds
entries.abstract: The velocity dispersion-size relation of molecular clouds, $σ_v = C\,(R/1\,{\rm pc})^γ$, has been reported with a power-law index ranging from $γ\approx$ 0.38 to 0.5 or higher, and a correspondingly varying normalization coefficient $C$, but the role of the intensity threshold in producing this scatter has not been quantitatively characterized. Using 4916 $^{13}$CO clouds identified with GDCluster (Liu & Du 2025) in the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting (MWISP) survey, we derive $γ$ and $C$ as functions of the intensity threshold $T_{\rm th}$. The index $γ$ increases monotonically with threshold, reaching a saturation value $γ_{\rm sat} \approx$ 0.56 for the full sample; splitting the sample by spiral arm gives higher values, $γ_{\rm sat} \approx$ 0.62 and 0.70. The normalization $C(T_{\rm th})$ declines monotonically, saturating at $C_{\rm sat} \approx$ 0.35 km/s and implying a surface density of ~46 Msun/pc^2 under a virial approximation. On the $γ(T_{\rm th})$ curve, $γ\approx$ 0.38 (Larson 1981) and $γ\approx$ 0.5 (Solomon et al. 1987) correspond to a low threshold ($T_{\rm th} \approx$ 1.2 K) and a near-saturation one (2.6 K), respectively, roughly consistent with the $^{13}$CO-equivalent boundary temperatures of these two studies. These two historically debated values, together with the broader $γ\approx$ 0.38-0.7 range reported in the literature, may largely reflect different positions along this single threshold-dependent curve and differences in sample composition. This threshold effect should therefore be considered when using Larson-type relations to assess the roles of turbulence and gravity. As an independent check, DBSCAN-identified $^{13}$CO and $^{12}$CO samples show the same monotonic trend in $γ$, though the curve shape differs quantitatively.

entries.title: Influence of Alfven wave turbulence dissipation in stellar winds of the Sun and M dwarfs
entries.abstract: The physics of M-dwarf stellar winds is increasingly being investigated within the framework of wave-driven models. In the case of the solar wind, Alfven-wave turbulence (AWT) is believed to play a crucial role in heating and accelerating the plasma. In this study, we perform one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar and M-dwarf winds using a model that incorporates shock heating generated by mode conversion and treats AWT as an optional component. For the solar wind, we confirm that including AWT reproduces the observed predominance of outwardly propagating Alfven waves, supporting the role of turbulent dissipation in driving the wind. We further validate this AWT-driven solar wind directly against Parker Solar Probe observations, finding good agreement in both the location of the Alfven point and the level of the normalized cross helicity in the fast solar wind. In M-dwarf simulations, we find that AWT dominates the overall heating budget within the investigated parameter range. A parameter survey of coronal magnetic field strength reveals that the dependence of the mass-loss rate on Bcor differs qualitatively between cases with and without AWT, highlighting the importance of chromospheric dissipation. In the absence of AWT, the resulting mass-loss rates are broadly consistent with previous studies and observations. In contrast, when AWT is included, the mass-loss rate is significantly reduced because turbulent dissipation decreases the Alfven-wave (Poynting) flux entering the corona. These results suggest that the effects of chromospheric turbulence play a crucial role in modeling M-dwarf winds.

entries.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
entries.abstract: We present spectral and temporal properties of a faint thermonuclear X-ray burst observed from SAX~J1808.4--3658 by NICER. Unlike the previous analysis of the same burst \citep{2023ApJ...948..117C}, our analysis focuses on the persistent spectral evolution and changes in the accretion environment. Following a peak flux of approximately 5\% of the Eddington limit, the burst emission settled into a stable state characterized by a temperature of 0.46 keV and a flux 14\% greater than the pre-burst value in the tail. Although the observation was truncated, it resumed after 3 hours, revealing that the source flux returned to its pre-burst level. Our spectral fitting results indicate that at the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission. Fitting the persistent spectra also reveals an increase in the visible fraction of the neutron star's surface from 25\% to 41\% during the period from 100 s to 550 s after the burst, suggesting a change in the disk structure (the height or the inner radius). The spectral evolution suggests a transient reorganization of the inner accretion flow during the burst peak, followed by partial recovery as the burst flux declines.

entries.title: Revisiting the Neutrino Emission and Physical Parameter Constraints from Time-Resolved Spectra of Gamma-Ray Bursts
entries.abstract: The non-detection of neutrinos associated with gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) has placed significant constraints on the physical parameter space of GRB jet models. However, most of these constraints have been derived using the time-integrated spectra. In this paper, we adopt time-resolved spectra, which provide a more detailed description of the prompt emission spectral structure, to calculate the neutrino emission, and investigate how they affect the constraints on GRB physical parameters. By selecting three GRBs (i.e., GRBs 090902B, 110721A and 080916C) whose spectra are composed of different components (e.g., thermal, thermal + non-thermal, and non-thermal), we find that the expected neutrino event numbers from the summed time-resolved spectra are lower than those from the time-integrated approach in the region of relatively low dissipation radius $R$ and bulk Lorentz factor $Γ$, while the opposite trend is found at high $R$ and high $Γ$. Moreover, we also use GECAM-C data to calculate the neutrino emission of the brightest GRB 221009A, and find that the expected number of neutrino events calculated from the summed time-resolved spectra is approximately three times that from the time-integrated spectra in the high-$R$ and high-$Γ$ regime. More details of constraints on the physical parameters are also discussed. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved spectra for future GRB neutrino studies.

entries.title: A Failed Filament Eruption and Associated Active Region Heating Driven by External Magnetic Reconnection
entries.abstract: We investigate a failed filament eruption and associated coronal heating in NOAA Active Region 12353 on 2015 May 23, focusing on the relationship between magnetic confinement and external reconnection. Coordinated observations from the Goode Solar Telescope and the Solar Dynamics Observatory, together with nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, allow us to trace the event from the merging of two low-lying filamentary structures to the failed eruption of the resulting elongated filament. Before the rapid rise, the modeled flux rope had entered a regime susceptible to kink instability, while low-atmospheric internal reconnection had already occurred; both may have contributed to the initial acceleration. The rising flux rope remained below the torus instability threshold and was confined by a strong, asymmetric overlying field that compressed it against the overlying loops. An elongated interface brightening, bidirectional plasmoid-like motions, newly brightened loop systems, and progressive weakening of the filament are consistent with external reconnection that changed the magnetic connectivity, removed magnetic flux from the rope, and disrupted its coherent structure. Differential emission measure analysis indicates that the external reconnection heated the active region loop system. A transient, localized structure with high-temperature emission was observed at the interaction interface, consistent with the expected location of a current sheet associated with external reconnection. These results suggest that the strong confining field halted the filament eruption and sustained the interface compression required for current sheet formation, enabling external reconnection to disrupt the flux rope and heat the active region loop system.

entries.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
entries.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ($M \gtrsim 2\ M_{\odot}$) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period $P\approx 1218\pm3$ days and a comparatively low eccentricity $e\approx 0.09\pm0.01$ (with $1 σ$ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from {\it Gaia} DR2 and DR3 catalogues, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle $i\approx73^{\circ}\pm11^{\circ}$. The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8--2.8 $M_{\odot}$ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of $2.20^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ $M_{\odot}$. This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

entries.title: Moving Beyond the DRW Model: Learning Quasar Variability with Generative Models
entries.abstract: The optical continuum variability of quasars is often described by a damped random walk (DRW) model, with characteristic damping timescales $τ_{\rm DRW}$ of hundreds of days and amplitudes $σ_{\rm DRW}$ of $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ magnitudes. This model has been widely used as a null hypothesis to assess the significance of periodic signals in quasar light curves in the search for supermassive black hole binaries, the significance of extreme quasar variability like tidal disruption events (TDEs) and changing-look (CL) quasars, or to model time lags in reverberation mapping. However, the DRW model is known to be incomplete, and an incorrect null hypothesis can lead to biased significance estimates. We investigate the impact of such null-hypothesis mis-specification on the detection of periodic signals in synthetic quasar light curves and introduce the generative model Nullasar, capable of learning quasar variability directly from time-series data. We demonstrate that Nullasar, trained with flow matching, can learn delicate statistical properties of stochastic light-curve variability without explicitly assuming any noise model. We further demonstrate that Nullasar can learn correlated distributions of noise parameters and generate new light-curve realizations from a range of deviations from the Gaussian DRW noise model, approximating parametric descriptions of stochastic processes. When used as a null hypothesis for detecting periodic signals in synthetic light curves, Nullasar performs comparably to fitting the correct DRW model to each light curve, and outperforms parametric fitting when the variability follows a more flexible AR(2) model. Finally, we identify practical limitations, including sensitivity to contamination of the training set by non-null signals, and show that projecting the conditioning vector of the model onto its leading principal components largely mitigates it.

entries.title: Prospects for probing supermassive binary black holes in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei via microlensing effects
entries.abstract: Gravitational microlensing in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei (AGNs) provides a powerful probe of accretion-disk structure and may offer a unique opportunity to identify sub-parsec supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) through distinctive signatures. Upcoming wide-field surveys are expected to discover a large sample of strongly lensed AGNs, a fraction of which may host SMBBHs detectable via microlensing. In this paper, we employ semi-analytic models to assess the detection prospects of sub-parsec SMBBHs in lensed AGNs, focusing on systems with resolvable multiple images suitable for microlensing analysis. Accounting for galaxy-scale strong-lensing statistics, and including the cluster-lensing contribution as an optimistic statistical extension, we estimate that up to approximately 87 such systems could be spatially resolved by individual upcoming surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin), Euclid, China's Space Survey Telescope (CSST), and the Roman. For the Rubin WFD survey, we estimate that periodic oscillations in microlensing light curves could identify $\sim0.12-0.68$ short-period ($<5$\,yr) binaries, whereas diagnostics based on the reconstructed size-wavelength relation apply to a broader population, potentially identifying $\sim0.4-5.3$ systems, depending on the model assumptions. CSST, Euclid, and Roman may also reveal up to $10.6$, $8.9$, and $1.2$ systems exhibiting size-wavelength features, and $2.3$, $1.9$, $0.3$ systems showing periodic oscillations, which should be regarded as imaging-selected candidates whose microlensing-based identification requires adequate time-domain follow-up, including cadence, monitoring baseline, photometric precision, and reliable time-delay measurements. Our results show that strongly lensed AGNs provide a promising, though observationally demanding, pathway for finding candidate SMBBHs via microlensing.

entries.title: Evolutionary Characteristics of the Solar Coronal Rotation: Revealed by a Century of Observations
entries.abstract: The 10.7 cm radio flux time series from 1874 May 9 to 2017 June 30, the longest available observational proxy of the solar corona, is used to systematically investigate the multi-scale evolution of coronal rotation period lengths (RPLs) using wavelet analysis and linear regression. Throughout the time interval considered, the coronal rotation is characterized by a dominant synodic period of approximately 26.72 days, which varies in a complex manner with the advancing solar cycle. The relationship between the coronal RPLs and sunspot number (SN) changes over time: anticorrelation during 1874.9-1943.1, correlation during 1943.1-1958.2, anticorrelation during 1958.2-1987.4, and correlation during 1987.4-2016.9. Overall, RPLs show a negative correlation with SN, but their relationship is complex. This scenario is reflected in the phase dependence of the RPLs on the solar cycle. The variation of RPLs is complex, but a distinct pattern emerges: during weak activity phases, coronal rotation is slower, whereas during strong activity phases (approximately years 3 to 6 of the solar cycle), it becomes faster. Several statistically significant periods are detected in RPLs. Cross wavelet transform and wavelet coherence further confirm that the complex evolutionary pattern of RPLs fundamentally results from the combined modulation of two factors: the direct and dominant effect of the ubiquitous small-scale magnetic fields on the coronal rotation, and the modulation of the entire solar atmospheric rotation by the solar magnetic activity level.

entries.title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
entries.abstract: Whether all fast radio burst (FRB) sources repeat, or whether some produce only a single burst, remains an open question. Using 3,950 bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure how the numbers of apparently single and repeating sources change with observing time, correcting for the declination-dependent, beam-weighted exposure and possible variations in the detection rate. Both source counts increase approximately linearly over 300--44,000~hr, as $N_{\rm s}\proptoΔt^{0.98\pm0.02}$ for single sources and $N_{\rm r}\proptoΔt^{1.06\pm0.14}$ for repeaters. Consequently, the observed repeater fraction remains nearly constant at $2.6^{+0.4}_{-0.6}\%$. We interpret these results using population models that account for a distribution of detected burst rates and temporal clustering. The source counts are reproduced by a population spanning a range of rates, including sources expected to produce approximately one detectable burst over the observing time. Its detected burst rates follow a distribution close to $r^{-2}$ over 0.01--1.5~hr$^{-1}$. The burst timing and burst multiplicities provide additional constraints. Among 77 repeaters, only 6 have their first two detected bursts within a single CHIME transit, the median interval between them is 101 days, and 31 of the 52 repeaters with at least three bursts have five or more. These observations support this population and favor moderately clustered emission (Weibull shape $k\simeq0.5$) and active phases lasting months to about a year. Our results are consistent with both a single population of repeaters whose rate distribution steepens below the range probed by CHIME and a mixed population that includes genuinely one-off sources. Thus, the current data do not require a one-off population, but cannot exclude one. Longer observing baselines are needed to distinguish these possibilities.

entries.title: Detection of 2 MeV spectral bump and ~40 MeV emission line from GRB 221009A
entries.abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are the most energetic transients in the Universe, but prompt MeV--sub-GeV observations remain challenging with current gamma-ray observatories. Here, using unsaturated HEPP-H measurements on board CSES-01 and cross-calibrating with likewise unsaturated GECAM-C data, we reconstruct the continuous spectral evolution of GRB 221009A over 2--255 MeV. We identify an unusual spectral bump at $\sim$2 MeV in the first light-curve peak. We also confirm a narrow emission line whose energy decreases from $\sim$40 MeV following a $t^{-1}$ evolution, and whose flux shows a ``rise-then-fall'' profile, implying weak emission from the central jet. These findings hint that a magnetically dominated, central-empty jet exists in the BOAT.

entries.title: Cosmic Ray Reacceleration and Gamma-Ray Emission via the Cloud-Wind Interaction in the Galactic Halo
entries.abstract: The interaction between cosmic rays (CRs) and multiphase gas in the Galactic halo may play an important role in shaping the hard gamma-ray spectrum of the Fermi bubbles. We investigate the interaction between a hot Galactic wind and a cold, dense gas clump with a relative velocity of $300\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ using two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations coupled with momentum-dependent CR transport. The system produces a bow shock and wind reacceleration region downstream, where the wind flow is faster than the initial velocity. For a CR pressure comparable to the gas pressure (CR-rich), the wind acceleration and turbulence behind the clump are enhanced. When CR pressure is dynamically weak, strong gas compression leads to significant CR spectral hardening. In contrast, for the CR-rich case, CR pressure gradients weaken the gas compression and suppress further CR reacceleration. We estimate the gamma-ray intensity from CRs, and find that reaccelerated CRs penetrate the dense clump and enhance hadronic gamma-ray emission. The gamma-ray intensity reaches $\sim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$ in the 1--10 GeV band, and the gamma-ray spectra become significantly harder, consistent with the Fermi bubbles' emission. These results suggest that an ensemble of dense gas clumps interacting with the Galactic wind may contribute to the gamma-ray emission of the Fermi bubbles.

entries.title: The SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project: Short Lags in the COSMOS Field
entries.abstract: We present the first reverberation mapping (RM) measurements in the COSMOS field included in the SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project. Using $\sim$6 months of plate-based spectroscopy (from late 2020 to mid-2021) and accompanying ZTF+DECam \emph{gri}-band photometric light curves, we analyze the variability of over 250 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) out to $z \sim 3$. We successfully recover reliable $\lesssim$ 200d time lags for 22 AGNs ($z \lesssim 2.5$) in H$α$, H$β$, MgII, or CIV, using a combination of multiple lag detection methods and significance tests. Our measurements are consistent with the radius-luminosity relations from recent large-scale RM programs, providing measured masses of $10^{7-9} M_{\odot}$ for these AGNs. These results and upcoming long-baseline SDSS-V spectroscopy lay the groundwork for large-sample AGN studies in conjunction with other facilities covering the COSMOS field, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and Roman Space Telescope.

entries.title: Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function
entries.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $Λ$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

entries.title: Enhancing Graviton--Photon Conversion through Galactic Magnetic Turbulence
entries.abstract: Plasma dispersion suppresses coherent graviton-photon conversion over astrophysical distances. We show that Galactic magnetic turbulence enables phase matching by compensating the plasma-induced mismatch, allowing matched magnetic modes to contribute coherently. In the long path limit, the ensemble-averaged conversion probability grows linearly with propagation distance in the phase matched regime and is governed by the projected magnetic power spectrum. Applied to photon background observations, this mechanism yields characteristic strain limits that are stronger than previous Galactic conversion bounds in the inertial range phase matching window, with improvements of up to two orders of magnitude.

entries.title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
entries.abstract: We investigate the potential nuclear de-excitation $γ$-ray line emission from low-energy cosmic rays (LECRs) in the Vela SNR region, one of the nearest and most angularly extended core-collapse supernova remnant (SNR) complexes. We calculate the MeV line emission from Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A using the TALYS nuclear reaction code, considering both direct and inverse interactions between the accelerated particles and the nuclei interior to the SNRs. The proton spectra are constrained by GeV--TeV $γ$-ray observations under the hadronic assumption, while a broad range of spectral indices is explored to account for the poorly constrained LECR population. We find that Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs. The integrated fluxes of the prominent 1.63 MeV $^{20}$Ne, 4.44 MeV $^{12}$C and 6.13 MeV $^{16}$O lines are approximately $1.3\times10^{-10}$ -- $1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$ -- $5.6\times10^{-7}$ and $1.6\times10^{-10}$--$2.6\times10^{-7}$ $\rm ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}$, respectively, over the explored proton spectra. We compare the predicted line emission with both the diffuse Galactic MeV continuum and local source-related continuum emission. In our background estimate, diffuse Galactic emission is the dominant component, while inverse Compton emission from pulsar wind nebula Vela X constitutes an additional local continuum component. The relatively low diffuse background toward Vela compared with the Galactic Center makes this region a promising target for future MeV $γ$-ray observations. Such observations could provide direct constraints on the LECR population and particle acceleration in this complex SNR region.

entries.title: UOCS. XVI. Census of post mass-transfer binaries across various evolutionary phases in M67
entries.abstract: M67 is a well-studied, solar-metallicity, old open cluster that hosts a diverse set of exotic stellar populations formed via mass transfer (MT). While Case A, B, and C MT systems have been individually examined in several clusters, a comprehensive investigation of all MT types across different evolutionary stages within a single cluster remains limited. This study aims to detect the presence of post mass-transfer systems using two different methods and thereby obtain a holistic view of binary evolution and mass-transfer mechanisms prevalent in M67. We constructed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for 141 UV-detected stars in M67 using far-UV data from AstroSat/UVIT, combined with archival data from Swift/UVOT, GALEX, Gaia, 2MASS, WISE, and other sources. Furthermore, we performed a detailed chemical abundance analysis of cluster members using high-resolution spectroscopy from the GALAH DR3+ survey. We identified 11 new MS+WD binaries with previously undetected hotter companions, effectively doubling the known MS+WD binary population in M67. This includes five confirmed ELM WDs with orbital periods of 100-200 days and no chemical peculiarities, confirming Case A or B post-MT systems.
